title: Stripping a padded string
statement: For every binary string $u$ and every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, stripping the string formed by appending a $1$ and then $k$ zeros to $u$ returns $u$.
replaced:
Let $\mathrm{strip}$ be the partial map on binary strings defined by:
$\mathrm{strip}(\varepsilon)$ is undefined, and for a bit $b$ and a string $v$,
$\mathrm{strip}(bv) = b\,\mathrm{strip}(v)$ when $\mathrm{strip}(v)$ is defined,
while otherwise $\mathrm{strip}(1v) = \varepsilon$ and $\mathrm{strip}(0v)$ is
undefined. Then for every binary string $u$ (possibly empty, possibly containing
$1$s) and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{strip}(u\,1\,0^k) = u$.
